{{< include ../exercise-header.qmd >}}

::: {#exr-ape-teach-spoon}
Consider a function `Total_Cost(Units, Unit_Price)`. You create two slices of this function to understand the behavior:

- Slice A: You hold `Unit_Price` constant at $10 and vary `Units` from 1 to 100.
- Slice B: You hold `Units` constant at 100 and vary `Unit_Price` from $10 to $1.

What is the geometric shape of the slice plots in Slice A and Slice B?

```{mcq}
#| label: ats-1-clws
a. Slice A is curved; Slice B is curved. [hint: Sorry. Focus on Slice A to see why. The output of the function along this slice will be $10 times Units. This is just the same() function with the output scaled by $10. The same() function is not curved.]
b. Slice A is linear; Slice B is linear. [correct]
c. Slice A is linear; Slice B is horizontal. [hint: A horizontal function means the output is constant regardless of the value of the input. But in slice B the output will vary from $1000 to $100.]
d. Slice A is vertical; Slice B is linear. [hint: But in Slice A you are varying Units when making the slice plot. The total cost will be Units x 10.]
```

:::
